data.title: Lucid teases upcoming Cosmos SUV in new video
data.description:
Lucid has showcased its upcoming EV in a video. The crossover SUV named Cosmos made a brief appearance at the end of the clip.

Lucid fans have caught a glimpse of the company’s next car. In a video shared on X, the automaker inserted a picture of the rear of the new Cosmos. The 96-second clip starts with a branding message before devoting about 10 seconds to the electric automobile.

The car in the video is mostly concealed by strategically engineered shadow. It carries the LUCID lettering on the rear illuminated in red, flanked on either side by a thin taillight. Other details that can be gleaned about the upcoming model include the sloping rear window and a roof fin.

That is how far Lucid revealed in the teaser. While the video shows no model name, Lucid is expected to launch the Cosmos next. It is a midsize SUV built on Lucid’s 800-volt, 69 kWh battery platform, named Atlas. Company CEO Silvio Napoli has claimed the car will have a driving range exceeding 400 miles.

The Cosmos will slot below both the Air sedan and Gravity SUV in price. It is expected to start around $50,000, making it Lucid’s most affordable vehicle. The latest update on the SUV is that it is undergoing validation, durability testing, crash certification, and cold-weather testing in New Zealand.

Attendees at Lucid’s Investor Day in March saw the Cosmos’ body-in-white validation model, but no photos made it online because Lucid confiscated phones. However, a camouflaged prototype appeared in public beside a Tesla Model Y a few months later.

Lucid promised to reveal the Cosmos in summer, but the timeline has obviously changed. Production has also moved to 2027, and it will be the first car produced at the company’s AMP-2 plant in Saudi Arabia.

data.title: Tesla officially announces November 20 launch date for Argentina
data.description:
Tesla has officially announced its launch date in Argentina, confirming it will enter the South American market on November 20.

The announcement came from Tesla’s official Latin American account on X on Friday, which shared a short video confirming the date with the message, “We arrived in Argentina on November 20.”

The confirmation comes just one day after we reported that Tesla would open its first location in Argentina at Unicenter, located in Martinez, Buenos Aires province toward the end of November.

According to Cencosud, the location will feature two Tesla vehicles on display on Level 1 of the shopping centre, allowing visitors to explore the company’s electric cars in person. A dedicated test-drive area is also planned, with ten vehicles available for test drives.

With the launch just weeks away, Tesla is also preparing additional facilities in Argentina. These include a Service and Delivery centre in Munro, along with other showroom locations in Belgrano and Alcorta Shopping.

Tesla has also secured changes to Argentina’s tariff-free import quota rules, allowing it to import electric vehicles manufactured in China without customs duties. The company also signed an agreement earlier this year with YPF to develop electric vehicle charging infrastructure.

The launch continues Tesla’s expansion across South America, following its entry into Chile, Colombia and Uruguay over the past few years.

data.title: Canadian YouTuber Linus Tech Tips Tests Tesla FSD
data.description:
Canadian tech YouTuber Linus Sebastian has put Tesla’s Full Self-Driving (FSD) (Supervised) system to the test, experiencing impressive performance. However, it wasn’t all positive, as the YouTuber had a concerning intersection incident forced him to intervene.

According to a video published by Linus Tech Tips on Thursday, Sebastian is swapping vehicles with colleague Colton for 30 days, borrowing his Hardware 4 (HW4) Tesla Model 3 while handing over his Porsche.

Sebastian, who runs the Canadian technology channel with approximately 16.9 million subscribers, has previously described himself as a Tesla skeptic. Having recently tested comma.ai’s driver assistance technology, Sebastian wanted to experience Tesla’s system firsthand using a newer Model 3 equipped with HW4.

His initial impressions were positive, particularly with how the vehicle handled everyday driving without requiring steering inputs.

“I have not touched the steering wheel one time, though,” Sebastian remarked during the drive.

However, things took a concerning turn later in the video around the 26 minute mark when the Model 3 approached an intersection. According to Sebastian, the vehicle signalled right before continuing straight through the intersection while another driver was turning left, prompting him to brake and disengage FSD.

Although it is worth noting the problem may have been the car was driving without a destination programmed into navigation.

He subsequently took a moment to decompress, explaining that FSD’s earlier performance had made him less prepared to intervene than with comma.ai.

Despite the incident, Sebastian remained impressed with the return journey, describing it as “pretty darn impressive on the way back” with zero interventions until reaching the wrong parking lot.

You can watch the full video below.

data.title: 2027 Toyota RAV4 Plug-in Hybrid gets NACS and DC fast charging
data.description:
Toyota has announced that the 2027 RAV4 Plug-in Hybrid will come standard with a North American Charging Standard (NACS) port, expanding access to Tesla’s Supercharger network and adding DC fast charging capabilities.

NACS and faster charging come standard

According to Toyota, all four Plug-in Hybrid (PHEV) trims will receive the new charging port, along with an upgraded 11 kW onboard AC charger.

The NACS port will allow owners to charge at compatible Tesla Superchargers without requiring a separate adapter, making longer trips more convenient. Toyota has also relocated the charging port to the driver’s side of the vehicle, making it easier to connect at charging stations.

While Toyota confirmed Level 3 DC fast charging support, the automaker did not disclose the maximum charging speed or battery capacity.

The changes apply to the U.S. market, with Toyota Canada yet to announce Canadian pricing or specifications for the 2027 RAV4 Plug-in Hybrid.

Electric range reaches up to 84 km

The 2027 RAV4 PHEV uses Toyota’s sixth-generation plug-in hybrid system, combining a 2.5-litre four-cylinder engine with electric motors to produce 321 horsepower and standard all-wheel drive.

Electric-only range varies by trim, with the SE offering up to 84 km (52 miles), followed by the XSE at 80 km (50 miles), Woodland at 74 km (46 miles), and GR SPORT at 72 km (45 miles).

The Woodland trim also receives revised suspension components and increased ground clearance, now measuring approximately 231 mm (9.1 inches), compared to 206 mm (8.1 inches) previously.

U.S. pricing and launch timing

U.S. pricing starts at US$42,100 for the RAV4 PHEV SE, excluding destination charges. The regular hybrid starts at US$32,300.

Toyota says the hybrid models will reach U.S. dealerships later this year, followed by the Plug-in Hybrid lineup in early 2027.

data.title: Tesla patent describes tendon-like cables for underactuated robot fingers
data.description:
Tesla has published another robot-hand patent that builds on earlier filings showing how the Optimus V3 hand could mimic human muscles and tendons.

The application was filed in March 20 and published November 5, 2026. It describes underactuated fingers driven by a single motor that pulls one tendon-like cable, rather than packing a separate drive at every joint.

Essentially, the cable acts as a tendon. It runs along the finger rather than wrapping around each knuckle. The tip of the cable is thicker and sits loose in the fingertip until the motor pulls. Then it catches on a ledge and the finger curls. If one section hits something first, that part can stop while the rest keeps closing — the same idea as grabbing a mug without thinking about which knuckle bends first.

Each finger has two hinged parts: one closer to the palm and one at the tip. Small springs at the joints help keep the finger steady. Tiny magnets and sensors tell the robot how far each joint has bent. A curved surface between the sections is there so the metal cable can flex without snapping.

The drawings show the fingers on a humanoid robot, but the text doesn’t name Optimus or any other product. On Oct 27, 2026, the patent examiner pushed back on the claims as written. That’s common at this stage and usually means Tesla will tweak the wording before anything is approved.

Hands are still one of the hardest parts of a humanoid to get right. This design tries to cut parts and wear by keeping the cable off the joints and letting the finger’s shape do more of the work. The filing doesn’t give grip-strength numbers or say how long the cable should last, so it’s still unclear how much better this setup would be in the real world.

data.title: Tesla lowers Supercharger prices at 178 locations across Canada, but raises others
data.description:
Tesla has made another nationwide Supercharger pricing adjustment overnight, with charging rates changing at 281 locations across Canada. This time there are more price decreases than increases.

According to Supercharger pricing tracked by Drive Tesla, 178 sites saw decreases between Thursday and Friday, while 103 increases. The changes were identified across 290 Canadian Supercharger locations, with rates now ranging from $0.18 to $0.79 per kilowatt-hour (kWh) for Tesla owners.

Western Canada sees mixed pricing changes

In Alberta, Saskatchewan and Manitoba, most locations saw modest increases of around $0.02 to $0.04/kWh. Calgary climbed from $0.48 to $0.52, while Edmonton switched to peak and off-peak pricing.

British Columbia saw a mix of changes. Around Metro Vancouver, Tesla peak rates rose – Tsawwassen climbed from $0.30 to $0.37/kWh, Richmond from $0.33 to $0.39, Burnaby and Surrey’s King George Boulevard both from $0.32 to $0.37 – while off-peak at many of those sites dropped slightly lower.

Meanwhile several Interior and Vancouver Island locations became cheaper, with typical drops of about $0.02–$0.03/kWh.

Ontario leads with 89 price cuts

Ontario recorded 89 price decreases, including substantial reductions at Ajax, where Tesla peak fell from $0.50 to $0.38/kWh, and at Burlington’s Appleby Line, where peak dropped from $0.50 to $0.39. Pickering and Grimsby also saw Tesla peak cut rates from $0.50 to $0.38.

However, some Greater Toronto Area locations saw peak rates climb to $0.55/kWh – Burlington’s main site and Kitchener both moved from $0.50 to $0.55 – while Markham, North York, and Scarborough rose from $0.50 to $0.53.

Meanwhile, Quebec saw higher peak prices around Montreal, including Brossard increasing from $0.44 to $0.51/kWh, while many locations dropping by around $0.03/kWh.

Atlantic Canada also saw increases pushing prices even higher, with Digby, Nova Scotia rising to $0.77/kWh and Enfield reaching $0.79/kWh during peak hours, the highest Tesla rate nationally.

To find out how Supercharger pricing changed in your area, you can use our searchable Supercharger pricing tool below to compare November 5 and November 6 rates at their local charging station.

You can also check out our full Supercharger pricing tool, or our Tesla Trip Planner, which estimates your Supercharging cost based on current pricing.

data.title: Tesla discontinues the Cybertruck after just three years, raises prices in the U.S.
data.description:
Tesla is pulling the plug and discontinuing the Cybertruck just three years after the first delivery.

Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced the news on Friday, saying the automaker will begin winding down production around the middle of 2027, shifting factory capacity toward Cybercab.

Expectations were high

Expectations for the Cybertruck were sky-high when Tesla first unveiled the electric pickup in 2019, with estimates suggesting the company had accumulated as many as 2 million reservations ahead of its launch.

However, when deliveries finally began in late 2023, the Cybertruck arrived with a much higher price tag and lower range and towing capabilities than originally promised, disappointing many potential buyers.

The Cybertruck’s appeal also faced challenges beyond its pricing and specifications. Elon Musk’s increasingly prominent involvement in politics became another obstacle, particularly among buyers who disagreed with his political views.

Combined with the truck’s unconventional design and high price, these factors made it difficult for Tesla to turn the enormous early interest into sustained sales.

Sales came in far below the initial hype

Tesla has never officially published Cybertruck sales figures, lumping them in with the “Otherr Models” category. However, Cox Automotive estimated just 4,323 U.S. Cybertruck sales during the third quarter of 2026 and 11,586 through September.

Tesla reported 8,295 deliveries in its broader Other Models category during the third quarter, a 48% decline compared to the same period last year.

Tesla increases Cybertruck prices

While the Cybertruck will only be made for a few more months, those remainings units will now also cost more. According to Tesla’s U.S. Cybertruck configurator, prices increased by up to 9% following the announcement, while orders for the popular entry-level Dual-Motor AWD have been paused.

The Premium AWD now starts at US$92,490, while the Cyberbeast costs US$102,490. The unavailable Dual-Motor AWD is listed at US$82,490, after initially selling for $59,990.

The Cybertruck remains available to order in Canada with no price changes. The Premium All-Wheel Drive (AWD) starts at C$139,990, while the Cyberbeast starts at C$167,990.

Cybertruck technology lives on through Cybercab

Cybertruck lead engineer Wes Morrill also commented on the announcement, describing the electric pickup as a technology development platform whose work continues through Cybercab.

“Cybertruck was an incredible technology development platform and lives on through Cybercab,” Morrill wrote, thanking those involved in its development and the owner community.

In a separate reply early Friday, Musk added that “the Cybertruck fleet will be around for a long time.”

data.title: Hyundai Recalls Nearly More Than 29,000 Kona EVs Over Airbag Defect
data.description:
Hyundai has issued a new recall affecting nearly 38,000 vehicles in the United States, including the Kona Electric.

According to a National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) filing, the recall covers 29,058 Kona Electric vehicles from 2019 to 2023 and 8,843 Veloster N vehicles from 2019 to 2022.

No matching Transport Canada recall has been listed as of Friday morning.

The issue involves the Airbag Control Unit (ACU), which detects crash signals and controls the deployment of airbags and seat belt pretensioners.

Under certain driving conditions, data stored in the ACU can become corrupted if the system reboots or loses power while writing to its internal memory.

This can trigger the airbag warning light and deactivate the airbag system. As a result, the airbags may fail to deploy during a crash, increasing the risk of injury.

Hyundai estimates approximately 1% of the 37,901 recalled vehicles may have the defect.

According to Hyundai, the company identified 331 unique incidents in the U.S. However, no crashes, fires, or injuries have been linked to the issue.

To address the defect, Hyundai dealers will install a free ACU software update designed to preserve the last known valid data if a transfer is interrupted.

You can read the full NHTSA recall notice below.

NHTSA Part 573 Safety Recall Report 26V728Download

data.title: Geely’s Canadian debut could include two popular SUV models
data.description:
Geely could be preparing to launch the EX5 electric SUV and Starray EM-i plug-in hybrid in Canada, following its announcement of a Canadian launch in 2027.

According to a report from Automotive News Canada, Transport Canada has added two Geely assembly plants in China to its list of manufacturers pre-cleared to import passenger vehicles.

The facilities, located in Guiyang City and Taizhou City, produce the EX5 and Starray EM-i, suggesting both vehicles could be among Geely’s first Canadian offerings.

The EX5 is an all-electric compact SUV already sold in Australia, where prices range from approximately C$40,870 to C$44,764, according to the report.

It offers up to 475 km of range under the Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicle Test Procedure (WLTP), which would work out to about 407 km under EPA-equivalent estimates used in Canada.

Meanwhile, the Starray EM-i combines a 1.5-litre four-cylinder engine with either an 18.4 kWh or 29.8 kWh lithium iron phosphate battery.

Depending on the configuration, the report estimates an electric-only range of approximately 71 to 116 km and Australian pricing ranges from roughly C$36,500 to C$43,800.

Both models have already helped establish Geely in international markets, including Australia and Europe, although Canadian pricing and the initial model lineup have not been announced.

Geely has also been expanding its Canadian presence, including hiring for its Zeekr brand and registering a Canadian trademark for Lynk & Co.

In its official October 9 announcement, Geely said its first vehicles would reach Canadians in 2027, with a retail and service network currently under development.
